title: Bending light: Snell's law
subtitle: Wave speed changes at optical boundaries

learn.prompt: Light traveling in air strikes glass (n = 1.50) at an incident angle of 45°. Adjust the beam until the refracted angle matches Snell's law.
learn.hint: Snell's law: n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2). Here 1.00 x sin(45°) = 1.50 x sin(θ2), so sin(θ2) = 0.707 / 1.50 = 0.471. Taking arcsin gives 28.1°.
learn.explanation: Because glass is optically denser than air (higher index), light slows down and bends toward the normal line, resulting in an angle of 28.1°.

learn.prompt: When a light wave passes from air into a denser medium like water, why does the ray bend toward the normal?
learn.hint: Think about what happens to the wave fronts as they enter the new medium.
learn.explanation: Light travels slower in water than in air. As the wavefront enters at an angle, the side entering first slows down first, pivoting the beam toward the normal.

options.label: The wave slows down in the denser medium
The wave speeds up in the denser medium
The frequency of the light increases
The medium absorbs the perpendicular components

misconceptionMap.b: Light travels slower in denser media: v = c / n.
misconceptionMap.c: Frequency is determined by the source and does not change across a boundary.
misconceptionMap.d: Refraction is a speed change effect, not selective absorption.

check.prompt: Light strikes water (n = 1.33) from air (n = 1.00) at an angle of 30°. Set the refracted ray angle to satisfy Snell's law.
Light moving through glass reaches the boundary with air. If it successfully transmits into the air, which direction does it bend?
check.hint: Light speeds up when leaving glass for air.
check.explanation: Because n_air < n_glass, the light speeds up, bending away from the normal (larger angle).

options.label: Away from the normal line (larger angle)
It does not bend at all

misconceptionMap.a: Bending toward the normal occurs when entering a slower medium, not a faster one.
misconceptionMap.c: Refraction always occurs at non-zero incidence when refractive indices differ.
misconceptionMap.d: Refraction angles obey Snell's law, not fixed 90-degree rotations.

takeaway.title: Snell's law governs refraction
takeaway.body: When light crosses into a medium with a different optical density, its wave speed changes according to n = c / v. The ray bends toward the normal when slowing down (n2 > n1) and away from the normal when speeding up (n2 < n1).
